title: Final and complete writings
summary: An integrated writing is intended as a final expression of some or all agreed terms. A complete integration is also intended to contain the entire agreement within its scope.
notes:
Finality and completeness answer different questions. A writing may finally settle the price while leaving another consistent undertaking outside its scope. Determining what the parties intended requires the jurisdiction’s method for evaluating the writing and surrounding evidence. Gianni and Masterson illustrate different assessments of whether an alleged collateral agreement belongs inside the written instrument.

A merger clause states that the writing represents the whole agreement. It is evidence relevant to integration, but its legal effect depends on the governing rule and circumstances. A clause cannot be assumed to settle its own disputed adoption, as the CISG analysis in TeeVee Toons illustrates.
